claims.text: A 2-5 vol% fraction of coherent ordered B2 nanoprecipitates can be established in a continuous disordered BCC Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr matrix.
This nanoprecipitate architecture will give the Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr alloy yield strength above 1.5 GPa and room-temperature tensile ductility above 10%.
Using Hf, Ti, and Zr instead of W will make the proposed alloy less dense than traditional W-based RHEAs.
Equiatomic Hf20Mo20Ta20Ti20Zr20 can exist as a single-phase disordered BCC solid solution after vacuum arc melting and homogenization at 1200°C.
Solution annealing at 1200°C for 24 hours followed by water quenching will retain a single-phase BCC Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr structure.
Aging the solution-treated Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr alloy at 800-900°C will nucleate and grow coherent B2 nanoprecipitates.
Adding 0.5-1.0 at.% Al or Si will promote B2 ordering without producing brittle continuous networks.
The desired mediator is discrete coherent B2 precipitates dispersed in a continuous disordered BCC matrix.
Coherent precipitate interfaces facilitate dislocation transmission and relieve stress concentrations that otherwise cause premature crack initiation.
B2 nanoprecipitates obstruct dislocation motion and thereby provide precipitation strengthening.
Coherent B2 interfaces enable cross-slip, which enhances ductility.
An inverted microstructure of discrete B2 precipitates in a continuous BCC matrix avoids the poor ductility associated with a continuous ordered B2 matrix.
The treated alloy will have a density of approximately 10.0-10.5 g/cm3.
W-based RHEAs often have densities above 12 g/cm3.
Ta20Nb20Hf20Zr20Ti20 has a reported density of 9.94 g/cm3 and becomes a single-phase BCC solid solution after annealing at 1200°C for 24 hours.
Standard Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr RHEAs typically have room-temperature tensile ductility below 5% because of continuous B2 phases or brittle intermetallics.
Al or Si additions above 2 at.% may form brittle continuous B2 networks or Laves phases and negate ductility gains.
Replacing W with Hf, Ta, and Mo is necessary for density reduction, but the extent of replacement is limited by the need to maintain BCC stability.
Incoherent or semi-coherent precipitates could act as crack-nucleation sites.
Trace oxygen or TiO-like impurities may affect B2-phase stability in the proposed Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr system.

contradictions.description: The target family is Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr, but the baseline labels Ta20Nb20Hf20Zr20Ti20, which contains Nb instead of Mo, as an example of a standard Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr RHEA.

The predicted targets are >1.5 GPa strength, at least 10% ductility, and 10.0-10.5 g/cm3 density, whereas falsification requires <1.0 GPa, <5%, or >11.5 g/cm3. Outcomes that clearly miss the predictions could therefore escape falsification.
